newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Cut-throat pricing slashes Sphinx results.
newsitem.headline: Cut-throat pricing slashes Sphinx results.

text.p: NV Koninklijke Sphinx Gustavsberg said on Thursday cut-throat competition in the bathroom fittings market had pushed its first-half result into negative figures.
"The most important reason for the loss is the heavy price competition in the market for ceramic sanitaryware, showers and baths," Sphinx said in a statement.

The company earlier reported it had booked a 2.4 million guilder loss over the first six months of its 1996/97 financial year ended September 30. In the same period of 1995/96 it posted net profits of 14.5 million guilders.
The continued downturn on the German construction market and a shift in the company's product mix towards lower margin products had further eroded the bottom line, Sphinx said.
It said that after its failure to reach agreement on a merger with Switzerland's Keramik Laufen it had given greater priority to existing restructuring and cost-cutting measures.
In addition it had scaled back investments and was seeking to reduce its working capital, it said.
Sphinx said its ceramic sanitaryware division had seen margins shrink even further on the back of continued price-cutting and a deterioration in its product mix.
Margins and sales volumes were also pressured at its bath and showers division.
However, its special products unit boosted turnover and operating profits.
Sphinx said the ongoing malaise on its markets, particularly in Germany and France, meant earnings improvement would have to come from internal restructuring and cost-cutting measures.
Sphinx said it expected to post a modest profit from ordinary operations over the full year.
